title: Introduce Priority Capacity Sentinel and Tenant Mute Adapter to reduce regional surge cascades
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: During a recent cross-region surge incident we observed cascading failovers when a handful of noisy tenants suddenly consumed most of a region's admission capacity. This PR introduces a lightweight Priority Capacity Sentinel (PCS) and a Tenant Mute Adapter (TMA) that together estimate per-tenant consumable capacity and perform conservative, probabilistic soft-throttles (a "mute") to prevent single-tenant surges from triggering regional failovers.

Summary of changes: Adds a new estimator component that continuously computes a short-horizon capacity budget per tenant based on recent token/req distributions, current KV pressure, and node-level headroom. The estimator exposes a small API for the admission controller to query an admission probability. The Tenant Mute Adapter implements a safety-first soft-throttle that temporarily reduces admission probability for tenants that exceed their estimated moving budget and integrates with existing circuit state to avoid flip-flopping. A rolling window cooldown and exponential backoff ensure mute durations decay automatically.

Design notes: - PCS uses an EWMA over a 60s/5m window pair and factors in kv-cache pressure and memory pressure markers exported by the runtime. It intentionally underestimates to favor safety. - TMA is feature-flag guarded (feature flag: enable_priority_capacity_sentinel) and starts with a global default mute probability of 0.15 when a tenant is over-budget; operators can tune this per-tenant via the console. - We record metrics for estimated_capacity, over_budget_ratio, mute_probability, mute_events.count, and mute_events.duration_ms. Telemetry keys added under telemetry.priority_capacity.*. - Integration with regional failover: when PCS detects >80% of region admission consumed by top-3 tenants for longer than 90s, it emits a signal (priority_capacity.topk_pressure) that can be consumed by the regional failover conductor to avoid hard failovers and instead trigger cross-region gentle re-route.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover estimator edge cases (zero-traffic warmup, sudden spike, and bounded negative adjustments). Integration tests simulate synthetic tenant surges; observed that mute events reduced peak admission by ~30% in local sim and prevented circuit tripping in the region simulator. CI initially failed lint for a small formatting issue which is fixed in commit 3. We will gate rollout behind the feature flag and do a staged rollout: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over a week with canary metrics and an ops playbook added to docs/runbooks/ops/priority-capacity-sentinel.md.

Backward compatibility and rollback: The feature flag defaults to off; enabling is opt-in for now. Rollback is simply toggling the flag off (mute adapter is safe by design and does not persist state beyond short windows). If an emergency rollback is required, a one-line revert is documented in the runbook.

Operational notes: Added dashboards: telemetry.priority_capacity.overview and a per-tenant heatmap. Alerts: priority_capacity.topk_pressure firing for >5mins and mute_events.rate > 0.5/min will page SRE.

Related: ENG-3421 (capacity estimation PoC), ENG-3567 (regional surge incident follow-up).

Checklist: - [x] Estimator algorithm implemented and unit-tested. - [x] Tenant Mute Adapter implemented and integrated with admission controller. - [x] Metrics and dashboards added. - [x] Runbook and rollout plan added. - [x] CI green after lint fix.

Notes for reviewers: focus on admission invariants, potential latency impact of estimator queries, and telemetry cardinality. I kept estimator datapoints coarse to avoid high-cardinality explosion.

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: High-level LGTM. A couple asks: 1) add a unit test for the warmup path (no prior traffic), 2) confirm estimator query is async-safe in tight admission hot paths.
Priya Nair: Added warmup test and switched estimator cache accesses to RCU-style snapshot to avoid locking in the hot path (see commit d4e8f22).
Jin Park: Please ensure mute events are rate-limited per-tenant to avoid oscillation. Also validate metrics cardinality (we only want tenant id when explicitly enabled in the console).
Priya Nair: TMA now enforces a per-tenant mute-rate cap and exposes tenant-id tagged metrics only when account_tenant_metrics_enabled is true (default false).
Sofia Patel: Integration test looks good; did a local run with the sim harness and confirmed no circuit trips under 2x baseline surge. Approving pending CI green.
release_notes: Adds a feature-flagged Priority Capacity Sentinel and Tenant Mute Adapter to reduce single-tenant surge impact on regional capacity. Includes telemetry, dashboards, and an ops runbook. Rollout must be gated via enable_priority_capacity_sentinel.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive mute could increase tail latency for some tenants. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-tenant overrides, and per-tenant rate caps; feature-flag rollout and canary metrics. Emergency rollback via flag toggle.
deployment_instructions: Deploy chart bump in charts/redwood with feature flag disabled in main. Enable per-cluster via console/ops and monitor telemetry.priority_capacity.overview and mute_events.*. Follow runbook to scale the rollout.
notes: This PR is intended as a long-term safety net complementary to existing SLO enforcers and circuit breakers; it is not a replacement for per-tenant rate limits or tenant-level quotas.
